title: On hosts whose Stop hook closes the task, a task-verify check alone no longer obliges an agent-side hunch_task finish
context: Measured in the PILOT5 Gate A v5 transcripts: the finish ritual ran on 20/20 Hunch runs and cost roughly 65-115k tokens per run (including deferred-tool schema loads), while for verify-only runs the Stop hook already closes the task and shows the same verify evidence. The maintainer chose this on 2026-10-01 to cut per-task overhead without losing agent-reported applications.
decision: Keeps dec_0bf3bda2c1's conditional model (the prompt hook prints the verify launcher; no agent start call) with one change: on hosts whose Stop hook closes the task (HOST_CLOSES_TASK), a `task verify` check by itself no longer counts as 'used Hunch'. The agent calls hunch_task finish only when it made a hunch_* call on the task ID, acted on Hunch hook context, or has an application to claim; otherwise the Stop hook closes the task and renders the verify evidence. Hosts without a Stop hook keep the existing rule (verify counts, finish required). The finish wording stays consistent across the always-loaded block, MCP instructions and the prompt-hook task instruction.
consequences: Verify-only tasks on Claude Code and Codex end with no agent finish call; the Stop hook's card is the record.
Tasks that used hunch_* tools or have an application to claim still finish agent-side on every host.
alternatives_rejected: Keep the dec_0bf3bda2c1 rule unchanged (verify counts as use): every verify-only task pays a finish round-trip, plus a tool-schema load on hosts with deferred tools, for a card whose evidence the Stop hook already shows.

Remove the agent-side finish entirely and rely on the Stop hook: rejected again (as on 2026-09-20). It loses agent-reported applications and the card in the final response, which the host-side notice cannot supply.
Apply the change to every host: hosts without a Stop hook have nothing else that closes the task or shows the evidence, so they must keep the finish.
